body:
CLAIM: PT/SLP/OT therapy furnished by the SNF is a covered type of service for the patient's SNF stay; the patient was referred for PT.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "D.E. was referred to PT due to decreased strength and decreased ADLs due to illness."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50.3): "Physical therapy (PT), speech-language pathology (SLP), and occupational therapy (OT) services must be provided by the SNF"

CLAIM: Skilled PT assessment of rehabilitation needs applies to a patient with hip fracture and weakness.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "J.M. was referred to PT secondary to a fall with fracture of the left hip with weakness."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.2): "The skills of a physical therapist are required for the ongoing assessment of a patient’s rehabilitation needs and potential."

CLAIM: A submitted hospital stay of about 12 days would exceed the 3-day minimum, but it is only asserted by the parties.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "December 15, 2009, through December 27, 2009, stay"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §100): "as long as some portion of the stay included at least 3 consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: UNKNOWN whether SNF admission occurred within 30 days of discharge; no SNF admission date is given.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary’s SNF stay met the criteria for Medicare coverage"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.1): "even if the beneficiary’s SNF admission occurs within 30 days of discharge from the qualifying hospital stay"

CLAIM: UNKNOWN whether the inpatient admissions were medically necessary; the facts give no clinical details of the patients.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Those cases that appear to be routine, expected discharge within 24 hours"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §10): "Admissions of particular patients are not covered or noncovered solely on the basis of the length of time the patient actually spends in the hospital."

CLAIM: UNKNOWN whether an inpatient admission order exists; facts do not address it.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The medical record must contain information that documents the need for an inpatient level of care."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §10.2): "is therefore required for all hospital inpatient cases for hospital inpatient coverage and payment under Part A"

CLAIM: Facts are procedural only; nothing shows a qualifying 3-day hospital stay, so eligibility is UNKNOWN.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant filed a timely request for Council review (Form DAB-101), dated August 24, 2009, and received on August 26, 2009."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20): "the individual must have been an inpatient of a hospital for a medically necessary stay of at least three consecutive calendar days"

CLAIM: Patient was admitted to the SNF after a qualifying hospital stay for a condition treated there, meeting the post-hospital stay requirement.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "after a qualifying hospital stay for treatment of delirium, a urinary tract infection (UTI), and dehydration"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §100): "as long as some portion of the stay included at least 3 consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: Whether the level-of-care presumption applies is UNKNOWN since no case-mix classifier is stated.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "admitted to *** skilled nursing facility (SNF) on January 17, 2006"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.1): "there is a presumption that he or she meets the Medicare"

CLAIM: Assisted living residence can qualify as the home if the facility is not primarily engaged in medical or skilled care; facility's nature is UNKNOWN.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "nursing services provided to Medicare beneficiary at his place of residence, an assisted living facility"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30.1.2): "if he or she resides in an institution that is not primarily engaged in providing to inpatients"

CLAIM: Homebound status is not addressed by the facts.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "from February 29, 2004, through April 28, 2004, and August 27, 2004, through December 24, 2004."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30.1.2): "the patient must meet both criteria listed in section 30.1.1 above"

CLAIM: SNF care relates to a condition treated in the hospital (GI bleeding stay), but length of stay is UNKNOWN.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "re-admitted to * * * Health & Rehab Center (SNF) on December 11, 2008, following a hospital stay for gastrointestinal bleeding"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "the beneficiary must require SNF care for a condition that was treated during the qualifying hospital stay"

CLAIM: Skilled PT/OT is a covered type of SNF service, but dates at issue follow therapy discharge.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "She was discharged from OT on January 19, 2009, and from PT on January 22, 2009."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50.3): "Physical therapy (PT), speech-language pathology (SLP), and occupational therapy (OT) services must be provided by the SNF"

CLAIM: Care related to a terminal condition may fall under hospice rather than Part A; hospice status is UNKNOWN.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant does not contend that the SNF care at issue was unrelated to the beneficiary’s terminal condition."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.3.1): "Hospices contract with SNFs for services related to the beneficiary’s terminal condition."

CLAIM: Passages do not establish basic home health eligibility (homebound status, plan of care) for insulin-related nursing; facts do not address these.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "As the appellant acknowledges in its brief, the beneficiary tested blood sugar levels on her own."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.13): "The home health record must document the rationale for the blood draw as well as the results."

CLAIM: Skilled nursing observation example concerns catheters; the facts show no catheter, so this passage does not settle coverage of the service type.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The beneficiary was given Cipro for a urinary tract infection"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.7): "The need for the skilled services must be documented."

CLAIM: The hospital stay of Feb 12 to Feb 17 counts at least 3 inpatient days (admission day counted, discharge day not).

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary’s hospitalization from February 12 to February 17, 2010"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.1): "the day of admission, but not the day of discharge, is counted as a hospital inpatient day"

CLAIM: SNF care was for conditions treated in the hospital, with direct admission on discharge day, within 30 days.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "At the time of discharge from the hospital on February 17 (for admission to the SNF)"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "the beneficiary must require SNF care for a condition that was treated during the qualifying hospital stay"

CLAIM: Hospital stay of 9 days followed by SNF admission the same day satisfies the post-hospital 3-day and 30-day requirements.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "first admitted to the SNF on August 25, 2011, following inpatient hospitalization from August 16, 2011, through August 25, 2011"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.2.1): "if initiated within 30 days after discharge from a hospital stay that included at least three consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: PT and OT furnished in the SNF are covered types of service.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Following readmission, the beneficiary received physical therapy (PT), occupational therapy (OT), and nursing services."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50.3): "Physical therapy (PT), speech-language pathology (SLP), and occupational therapy (OT) services must be provided by the SNF"

CLAIM: Skilled therapy is a covered type of SNF service, but whether this patient's therapy needed a qualified therapist is not settled by the facts.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "rehabilitation services to promote safety and maximize functional independence"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4): "Therapy services are considered skilled when they are so inherently complex that they can be safely and effectively performed only by"

CLAIM: UNKNOWN whether an active written treatment plan based on an initial PT evaluation existed.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "sustained a fall in the facility on September 2, 2008"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.1): "The services must be directly and specifically related to an active written treatment plan"

CLAIM: PT to teach a beneficiary safe use of a stair lift/transfers and set up a maintenance program is a covered type of home health therapy.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant further asserts that the skilled therapist was needed to teach the beneficiary how to safely transfer to and from the lift."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.2.1): "The instruction of the beneficiary or appropriate caregiver by a qualified therapist regarding a maintenance program is covered"

CLAIM: PT teaching safe stair navigation is reasonable and necessary where stairs are impaired.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "difficulty navigating stairs in his home due to fatigue, pain and abnormality of gait"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.2.2): "Physical therapy would be reasonable and necessary to teach the patient to climb and descend stairs safely."

CLAIM: A skilled nursing visit to evaluate infection symptoms and report to the physician is a covered type of service.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "He had a recurrence of urinary tract infection around mid-point"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.7): "The skilled nursing visit to change the catheter and to evaluate the patient would be reasonable and necessary"

CLAIM: Routine ostomy care is not skilled, so only the complication-related visits fit; which visits were routine is UNKNOWN.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "His bowel and bladder functions are maintained by colostomy and urostomy."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30): "changing the colostomy bag does not become a skilled nursing service when the nurse provides it"

CLAIM: Home health requires being confined to the home, physician care, plan of care and a skilled need; the facts do not address any of these.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the appellant asserts that coverage is available for home health aide or skilled nursing services on a part-time basis"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30): "A patient must meet each of the criteria specified in this section."

CLAIM: Hours claimed (28 to 35 per week) fall within the part-time/intermittent limits only if daily hours are under 8; daily hours are UNKNOWN.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "whether Medicare covered at least 28 hours and up to 35 hours of the home health services"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §50.7): "less than 8 hours each day and 28 or fewer hours each week"

CLAIM: Beneficiary entered the SNF directly after a hospital stay described as qualifying, for the cancer condition; this satisfies the prior-hospitalization conditions as alleged.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "both following a qualifying hospital stay"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "the beneficiary must require SNF care for a condition that was treated during the qualifying hospital stay"

CLAIM: Placement in a noncertified bed means payment depends on limitation-of-liability conditions; whether the facility has a participating distinct part SNF is UNKNOWN.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The beneficiary’s medical records indicate that she was placed in a noncertified bed at the appellant’s facility."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50): "the services may be paid under certain conditions, based on the limitation of liability provisions"

CLAIM: IRF care is covered only if each beneficiary meets specific IRF requirements; the facts give no beneficiary-level clinical or admission details.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "This appeal involves IRF services provided by the appellant to five beneficiaries on various dates between March 2003 and May 2004."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110): "Medicare requires determinations of whether IRF stays are reasonable and necessary to be based on an assessment of each beneficiary's individual care needs."

CLAIM: SNF admission followed an acute inpatient admission of about a week, within 30 days, for a post-hospital stay.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "On July 20, 2009, the beneficiary (age 88) was admitted to the acute psychiatric unit at Yale University for dementia"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.2.1): "if initiated within 30 days after discharge from a hospital stay that included at least three consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: Skilled nursing observation can cover patients with psychiatric needs, though such cases must be carefully documented.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary was closely monitored by the skilled nurses (multiple times each day)"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.2.3.2): "Skilled observation and assessment may also be required for patients whose primary condition and needs are psychiatric in nature"

CLAIM: Skilled nursing is covered when an individualized assessment shows an RN's skills are necessary; the nurse monitoring for pneumonia fits the service type.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "ongoing, frequent monitoring by the nursing staff"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.3): "Nursing services are considered skilled when they are so inherently complex that they can be safely and effectively performed only by"

CLAIM: IRF care is covered only if the patient meets all the listed IRF requirements; the facts do not show whether each requirement was met.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant billed Medicare for IRF services furnished to the beneficiary from July 17, 2003, through July 24, 2003."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110): "IRF care is only considered by Medicare to be reasonable and necessary under 1862(a)(1)(A) of the Social Security Act"

CLAIM: UNKNOWN whether a preadmission screening within 48 hours of IRF admission was done; facts give prior function and status on admission only.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Prior to the total knee replacement surgery, the beneficiary was independent with all of her activities"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110.1.1): "a preadmission screening is an evaluation of the patient’s condition and need for rehabilitation therapy and medical treatment"

CLAIM: Therapy must be reasonable and necessary; case shows functional decline but no determination that skilled need is met

CASE FACT QUOTED: "At the beginning of PT, D.E. required moderate assistance for all functional transfers."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.1): "The services must be reasonable and necessary for the treatment of the patient"

CLAIM: Qualifying 3-day hospital stay appears met by a 12-day stay, but SNF level of care and admission timing are not settled

CASE FACT QUOTED: "December 15, 2009, through December 27, 2009, stay at *** *** Hospital"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §100): "as long as some portion of the stay included at least 3 consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: Inpatient admission is not covered or noncovered by length of stay alone; the case gives no clinical facts on need for inpatient care

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The medical record must contain information that documents the need for an inpatient level of care."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §10): "Admissions of particular patients are not covered or noncovered solely on the basis of the length of time the patient actually spends in the hospital."

CLAIM: Admission directly after a qualifying hospital stay may trigger a presumption, but the case does not show the case-mix classification or level of care

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The beneficiary was admitted to *** skilled nursing facility (SNF) on January 17, 2006, after a qualifying hospital stay"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.1): "If the beneficiary is admitted to the SNF immediately following a 3-day qualifying hospital stay"

CLAIM: Coverage depends on whether the facility is primarily engaged in providing medical or skilled care; not established in the case

CASE FACT QUOTED: "nursing services provided to Medicare beneficiary at his place of residence, an assisted living facility"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30.1.2): "resides in an institution that is not primarily engaged in providing to inpatients"

CLAIM: Condition requiring SNF care must have been treated in the qualifying hospital stay; skilled need for the billed dates is not established

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The beneficiary was re-admitted to * * * Health & Rehab Center (SNF) on December 11, 2008, following a hospital stay for gastrointestinal bleeding."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "the beneficiary must require SNF care for a condition that was treated during the qualifying hospital stay"

CLAIM: Skilled observation and monitoring of drug actions is reasonable and necessary; nurses acted on blood sugar logs leading to insulin changes

CASE FACT QUOTED: "insulin dosage was adjusted numerous times during this period"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.1): "Skilled observation and monitoring of the drug actions is reasonable and necessary"

CLAIM: Hospital stay of 5 days meets the 3-day requirement

CASE FACT QUOTED: "hospitalization from February 12 to February 17, 2010"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.1): "In determining whether the requirement has been met, the day of admission, but not the day of discharge, is counted as a hospital inpatient day."

CLAIM: SNF care is for a condition treated in the qualifying hospital stay

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary was diagnosed with hematuria secondary to prostate enlargement"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "the beneficiary must require SNF care for a condition that was treated during the qualifying hospital stay"

CLAIM: Post-hospital timing is met by direct admission after a 9-day stay, but skilled need after therapy discharge is not settled

CASE FACT QUOTED: "following inpatient hospitalization from August 16, 2011, through August 25, 2011"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.2.1): "initiated within 30 days after discharge from a hospital stay that included at least three consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: Coverage turns on need for skilled care rather than improvement potential; case shows only appellant assertions

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant asserts that the beneficiary made steady progress throughout physical therapy"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4): "Coverage for such skilled therapy services does not turn on the presence or absence of a beneficiary"

CLAIM: Therapy is not necessary if expected results are insignificant; goals conceded met by Sept 11

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant also concedes that the beneficiary met her goals by September 11, 2008"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.1): "Physical therapy services are not reasonable and necessary and would not be covered if the expected results are insignificant"

CLAIM: Therapist visits solely to train aides are not billable, and skilled maintenance therapy requires individualized showing of need; not settled in case

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant agreed that setting up a maintenance program for the home health aides to take over was a goal"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.2.1): "visits made by skilled therapists to a patient's home solely to train other HHA staff (e.g., home health aides) are not billable as visits"

CLAIM: Skilled therapy covered when individualized assessment shows need; only appellant assertion of need shown

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant further asserts that the skilled therapist was needed to teach the beneficiary how to safely transfer to and from the lift."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.2.1): "skilled therapy services are covered when an individualized assessment of the patient"

CLAIM: Routine colostomy care is not skilled absent complications; here there were complications

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The beneficiary developed a fistula near the colostomy site."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30): "A patient with a well-established colostomy absent complications may require assistance changing the colostomy bag"

CLAIM: Complications requiring more frequent skilled care are covered with documentation

CASE FACT QUOTED: "He was hospitalized for several days in July 2007 for urosepsis and e.coli infection."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.7): "where there are complications that require more frequent skilled care related to the catheter, such care would, with adequate documentation, be covered"

CLAIM: Part-time or intermittent limit is under 8 hours daily and 28 hours weekly, up to 35 case by case; hours actually furnished not stated

CASE FACT QUOTED: "at least 28 hours and up to 35 hours of the home health services"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §50.7): "less than 8 hours each day and 28 or fewer hours each week"

CLAIM: Placement in a noncertified part of an institution may be paid under limitation of liability conditions; whether conditions are met is not settled

CASE FACT QUOTED: "she was placed in a noncertified bed"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50): "the services may be paid under certain conditions, based on the limitation of liability provisions"

CLAIM: IRF coverage depends on individual care needs assessment; no clinical facts in case

CASE FACT QUOTED: "were Medicare coverage criteria met for the IRF services at issue"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110): "Medicare requires determinations of whether IRF stays are reasonable and necessary to be based on an assessment of each beneficiary"

CLAIM: Skilled observation may be required for psychiatric needs

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary was closely monitored by the skilled nurses (multiple times each day)"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.2.3.2): "Skilled observation and assessment may also be required for patients whose primary condition and needs are psychiatric in nature"

CLAIM: Monitoring led to treatment changes

CASE FACT QUOTED: "On August 5, 2009, the psychiatrist reduced her Haldol from three to two times a day"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.2.3.2): "reasonable potential that skilled observation and assessment by a licensed nurse will result in changes to the treatment"

CLAIM: Pneumonia treated with monitoring

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary was diagnosed with pneumonia"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.3): "Nursing services are considered skilled when they are so inherently complex"

CLAIM: IRF care is reasonable and necessary only if all regulatory requirements are met; case does not show preadmission screening or therapy intensity

CASE FACT QUOTED: "moderate assistance supine to sit, sit to stand, sit to supine, bed to chair, chair to bed, commode transfers"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110): "IRF care is only considered by Medicare to be reasonable and necessary under 1862(a)(1)(A) of the Social Security Act if the patient meets all"

CLAIM: Medical-record documentation of patient condition and need for skilled therapy is present.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "At the beginning of PT, J.M. required moderate to maximal assist with functional mobility."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.2): "Documentation of the patient’s condition in the medical record must describe the circumstances which delineate the need for skilled rather than"

CLAIM: Nursing notes document skilled observation after the fall.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The nurses monitored J.M.’s condition including pupil size, alertness, signs and symptoms of pain and ability to follow commands."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.2.3.2): "The medical documentation must describe the skilled services that require the involvement of nursing personnel to promote the stabilization"

CLAIM: Hospital records for a 12-day stay were submitted as evidence of the qualifying stay.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The provider submits, as evidence of the three-day stay, hospital records concerning the beneficiary’s December 15, 2009, through December 27, 2009, stay"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §100): "as long as some portion of the stay included at least 3 consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: Medical evidence of ongoing skilled medication management is in the record.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "On at least thirteen occasions the beneficiary’s medications had to be adjusted due to fluctuations in his blood pressure and heart rate."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.1): "coverage would be determined based on a review of the medical evidence in the file"

CLAIM: UNKNOWN whether admission orders, certification or inpatient-need documentation exist; case facts only describe the appellant's arguments.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The medical record must contain information that documents the need for an inpatient level of care."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §10.2): "The signed physician certification is considered, along with other documentation in the medical record, as evidence that hospital inpatient service(s) were reasonable and necessary."

CLAIM: UNKNOWN: case facts are procedural only and contain no hospital stay or SNF transfer records.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant filed a timely request for Council review (Form DAB-101), dated August 24, 2009, and received on August 26, 2009."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20): "the individual must have been transferred to a participating SNF within 30 days after discharge from the hospital"

CLAIM: UNKNOWN: no case-mix classifier or length of the hospital stay is given, so presumption or level-of-care documentation is unsettled.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "admitted to *** skilled nursing facility (SNF) on January 17, 2006, after a qualifying hospital stay"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.1): "the beneficiary must receive an individual level of care determination using existing administrative criteria and procedures"

CLAIM: UNKNOWN: no certification or supporting medical records are described in the case facts.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The ALJ decisions concerned nursing services provided to Medicare beneficiary at his place of residence, an assisted living facility"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30.5.1.2): "documentation in the certifying physician or allowed practitioner’s medical records"

CLAIM: UNKNOWN: length of the hospital stay is not documented in the case facts.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The beneficiary was re-admitted to * * * Health & Rehab Center (SNF) on December 11, 2008, following a hospital stay for gastrointestinal bleeding."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "The beneficiary must have been an inpatient of a hospital for a medically necessary stay of at least 3 consecutive calendar days."

CLAIM: Therapy records end before the disputed dates of service beginning January 28, 2009; no records show skilled services on those dates.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "She was discharged from OT on January 19, 2009, and from PT on January 22, 2009."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50.3): "Physical therapy (PT), speech-language pathology (SLP), and occupational therapy (OT) services must be provided by the SNF"

CLAIM: Visit notes document skilled nursing monitoring and assessment.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the records dated within this period include numerous documented instances of changes in the beneficiary’s medication schedule"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.7): "The need for the skilled services must be documented."

CLAIM: Nursing visit documentation of physician contact and insulin dose changes is present (catheter policy only analogous; no venipuncture records described).

CASE FACT QUOTED: "On multiple occasions during this period, the nurses had the beneficiary see her doctor with her blood sugar logs"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.1.2.7): "where there are complications that require more frequent skilled care related to the catheter, such care would, with adequate documentation, be covered."

CLAIM: Hospital stay dates documented; Feb 12 to Feb 17 spans more than three inpatient days.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary’s hospitalization from February 12 to February 17, 2010"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.1): "the day of admission, but not the day of discharge, is counted as a hospital inpatient day"

CLAIM: Direct transfer to the SNF at hospital discharge is documented.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "At the time of discharge from the hospital on February 17 (for admission to the SNF)"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §10): "The beneficiary must also have been transferred to a participating SNF within 30 days after discharge from the hospital"

CLAIM: Qualifying hospital stay and same-day SNF admission are documented.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "first admitted to the SNF on August 25, 2011, following inpatient hospitalization from August 16, 2011, through August 25, 2011"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §20.2.1): "initiated within 30 days after discharge from a hospital stay that included at least three consecutive days of medically necessary inpatient hospital services"

CLAIM: UNKNOWN: written treatment plan and initial evaluation are not described; only the appellant's assertions about documentation appear.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The appellant asserts that the documentation of record, present throughout all levels of review, demonstrates the clear need for the skills of a physical therapist"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.1): "an active written treatment plan that is based upon an initial evaluation performed by a qualified physical therapist after admission to the SNF"

CLAIM: UNKNOWN whether the record delineates need for skilled rather than unskilled services.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the beneficiary demonstrated “slow but steady progress” reflecting gains in “safety, balance and overall functional mobility.”"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.4.1.2): "Documentation of the patient’s condition in the medical record must describe the circumstances which delineate the need for skilled rather than"

CLAIM: UNKNOWN: PT notes and certification are cited but their contents are not described, so documentation of each maintenance-program component is unsettled.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "Ex. 1, at 333 (physician certification of April 8, 2006), at 133 (PT notes of February 7, 2006)"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §40.2.2): "Each component of this process must be documented in the home health record."

CLAIM: Nursing documentation of complications supporting skilled need is present.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The nurses noted abscesses in the rectum."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30): "The medical condition of the patient must be described and documented to support the need for nursing skilled services"

CLAIM: Documented complications distinguish this from routine ostomy care.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The beneficiary developed a fistula near the colostomy site."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §30): "A patient with a well-established colostomy absent complications may require assistance changing the colostomy bag"

CLAIM: UNKNOWN: case facts give no visit logs, hours furnished or medical records, only the appellant's arguments.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "the appellant asserts that coverage is available for home health aide or skilled nursing services on a part-time basis"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.7 §50.7): "less than 8 hours each day and 28 or fewer hours each week"

CLAIM: Records show placement in a noncertified bed; no limitation-of-liability documentation is described.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "The beneficiary’s medical records indicate that she was placed in a noncertified bed at the appellant’s facility."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §50): "When patients who require SNF services are placed in a noncertified part of an institution which contains a participating “distinct part” SNF"

CLAIM: Direct admission after a qualifying stay is documented, but this does not cure the noncertified bed.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "On September 29, 2003, the beneficiary was admitted to the appellant’s nursing facility, REMH, immediately following her discharge from the hospital"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.1): "If the beneficiary is admitted to the SNF immediately following a 3-day qualifying hospital stay"

CLAIM: UNKNOWN: case facts contain no IRF medical records or individual assessments, only procedural history.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "This appeal involves IRF services provided by the appellant to five beneficiaries on various dates between March 2003 and May 2004."

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.1 §110): "Medicare requires determinations of whether IRF stays are reasonable and necessary to be based on an assessment of each beneficiary's individual care needs."

CLAIM: Detailed nursing, physician and psychiatric APRN documentation of monitoring is present.

CASE FACT QUOTED: "During the period from July 27, 2009, through August 11, 2009, the beneficiary was closely monitored by the skilled nurses (multiple times each day)"

POLICY QUOTED (MBPM ch.8 §30.2.3.2): "these cases must be carefully documented."
